findings.finding: c2's new sentence says a 'resources' that is not an object 'meets MC34 first'. MC34 (resources = c.get('resources') or {}) refuses only a falsy non-object: [], '', null, 0 or false give MC34's text. A truthy non-object, such as ['x'], 'x', 5 or true, in a container or an init container, makes check_manifest raise AttributeError at MC34, exactly as v3 and c1 do (my probes on PodInit). The README does not say that check_manifest can raise, so an oracle written from the README alone could expect MC34's refusal for resources ['x']. This is carried v3 behaviour, which item 3 keeps unchanged, and round 1 treated such raising as a NOTE (LPK1-C1-3). MC42's own new guard also covers a non-object 'resources', but MC34 makes that branch unreachable. The non-object 'limits' case is fixed as item 3 requires.

questions: Q-C2-1: confirmed, and (a), keep c2 as written. Take the profile v2 positive with the Pod's requests.cpu and limits.cpu both set to '500m' followed by one line feed, rehashed. It is schema-valid under the pinned bundle and the walker, because the cpu pattern ^[1-9][0-9]{0,6}m$ admits the trailing line feed and maxLength is 128. P01-P16 and P17 pass, and then int(cpu[:-1]) raises ValueError, so validate returns P99 in c2, as it did in c1. precondition is met. Admission v4 admits that Pod (A2 admit), because v4 checks no cpu form, so the profile is narrower than v4, not wider. P99 masks any later failure of the same document; with a wrong volumes echo, it still gives P99 and not P32. That is VPC's order, since the cpu read precedes P18-P22 and P30-P35. No other parsed document reaches validate's P99. Statically, every post-schema read in validate is of a schema-required member with a schema-fixed type. strptime failures map to P02, and canonical failures map to P01. int() accepts the trailing line feed for memory, ephemeral-storage and sizeLimit. So the cpu slice is the only conversion that can fail. Dynamically, 1408 leaf variants (307 schema-valid: a trailing line feed, Arabic-Indic and full-width digits, empty, zero, the 15-digit maximum, upper case, and integer bounds, with the requests and limits twins kept equal) and 419 structural edits (53 schema-valid: drop, duplicate or reverse items; delete members) reach P99 only through that cpu variant. 0 of the 66 vectors reach P99. precondition's P99 is reached only by arguments that are not a profile object with a binding namespace, which is the README's use (2). No document refuses with a specific VPC step while c2 gives P99. VPC refuses every step with one generic text ('invalid strict proxy profile data'), and the README maps P codes to its _require steps. The cpu read at VPC's line 191 is not such a step: it is the same unguarded int() inside the single catch, so P99 is the faithful code (wording note: LPK1-C2-2). Recommendation (a): mapping the failure to a P code now would add a rule that VPC does not have. A later successor could instead refuse a trailing line feed in every pattern, in both contracts together (LPK1-C1-2's option). That would make validate's P99 unreachable for parsed documents. The D5a oracle brief should carry this cpu case beside the lone surrogate.
